problems.title: Part A - Q1 Graph Creation & Q2 Graph Modification
problems.anchor_text: Part A – Graph Creation and Modification (30 pts) ... Q1: Graph Creation (15 pts) ... Q2: Graph Modification (15 pts)
subparts: Q1 (15 pts): create the undirected graph shown in the figure on rendered page 2 and show a visualization of it
Q2 (15 pts): from that graph remove node 1, edge (0,4) and edge (0,5); list the remaining connected components and visualize the remaining graph
problems.grouped_with_reason: Q2 operates directly on the graph constructed in Q1 ('Based on graph created in Q1'). Splitting them would let two workers transcribe the figure's edge list independently and produce contradictory graphs. They are one unit.

problems.title: Part B - Q3 Graph Creation & Q4 Graph Essentials
problems.anchor_text: Q3: Graph Creation (10 pts) ... Q4: Graph Essentials (30 pts)
subparts: Q3 (10 pts): build undirected graph from the attached edge-list file; report node count, edge count, number of connected components
Q4a (10 pts): largest connected component - report its node and edge count
Q4b (10 pts): visualize the second largest connected component
Q4c (10 pts): plot the degree distribution of the whole graph
problems.grouped_with_reason: Q4 is explicitly 'based on the created graph in Q3' and its answers (component sizes) are a direct continuation of the Q3 component count. Structural/component analysis is one coherent unit.

problems.title: Part B - Q5 Graph Measures
subparts: Q5a (10 pts): eigenvector centrality, report top-10 nodes
Q5b (10 pts): Katz centrality, report top-10 nodes
Q5c (10 pts): average clustering coefficient of all nodes; average Jaccard similarity of all connected node pairs
problems.grouped_with_reason: Q5's three parts are all centrality/similarity measures on the same graph and are naturally one unit. Split from p2 because Q5 shares only the (fully deterministic, file-defined) input graph with Q3/Q4 and needs no result computed in Q4; the graph construction convention is pinned identically in both briefs so the two workers cannot diverge.

uncovered: Rendered page 1 is the cover page (course header, Assignment Date / Submission Date / Student Name blanks). No question on it; handled by the master when assembling the final document, not assigned to a worker.
The administrative preamble on rendered page 2 (100 points total, independence statement, Canvas submission deadline Monday 09/14/2026) is instructions, not a question.
